acceptance.acceptance_criterion: Event resume, duplicates, cursor gaps, pagination, retention and artifact authorization pass reconnect and isolation cases
acceptance.observed_result: SQLModel event append_once survives restart, returns the original event for a repeated scoped key, and conflicts if that key is reused with changed content. Migration 008 adds its idempotency mapping separately and retains event history on downgrade/re-upgrade. Managed worker tests publish run.started and run.completed with run/submission/plan/attempt identity across report recovery. Headless and HTTP bounded history pages return the same scoped result; pagination advances over interleaved workspace events, and SSE reconnect and unknown-cursor behavior are covered. Memory, SQLite and PostgreSQL retention tests prune old events, return 410 for expired cursors, keep the highest-sequence anchor and preserve idempotency tombstones so a delayed publisher cannot recreate a pruned event. Managed deployment now enforces event-count retention per tenant/workspace on append and history reads, defaulting to 100,000 rows and preserving sequence continuity; focused memory, SQLModel and managed-backend tests passed 36 cases. The automatic policy also passed against isolated PostgreSQL 16.14, including expired-cursor and duplicate-retry 410 behavior after pruning. In-memory retry tombstones retain only digests and a cursor, not another payload copy.
acceptance.open_reason: Managed event history now has an enforced per-scope count policy, but keyed tombstones remain indefinitely to prevent expired retries from recreating events. Authorized artifact content downloads and the complete reconnect and cross-scope isolation campaign remain open.

acceptance.acceptance_criterion: Leases protect accepted/retry/replay inputs from retention; aborted uploads, orphans and expired inputs have bounded cleanup and stable outcomes

Abort is limited to staged uploads. The managed worker rejected the initial run before runtime startup, then executed retry, rerun and replay from the same finalized resource; four durable leases preserved reads beyond staging TTL. HTTP cleanup qualification verifies permission denial, caller-owner scoping, bounded batches, stable candidate counts and idempotent empty cleanup. The combined input-resource, CSV, HTTP, worker and migration suite passed 56 tests with no skips. PostgreSQL 16.13 multi-process lease-versus-cleanup qualification passed six trials, including both serialized orderings and four simultaneous races; no successful lease referred to deleted bytes. The clean Python 3.14.3 wheel smoke verified lease reads after backend restart.
